author: BBC News
description:
A UK space company has successfully tested a key part of a nuclear fusion rocket engine that could one day make journeys to Mars much faster.
 
Pulsar Fusion’s Sunbird rocket uses the same process that powers the Sun to create extreme heat and thrust, with engineers hoping it could cut travel times through space.
 
The technology is still in development, but the team says the breakthrough could help transform future missions to the Moon, Mars and beyond.

author: BBC News
description:
We look at what Number 10 has in store for Andy Burnham ahead of his first day as UK prime minister with two insiders who’ve been there with former prime ministers.

Lord Stewart Wood was an advisor to Gordon Brown and Lucia Hodgson was Boris Johnson’s deputy dire of communications.

They explain what the first day is like, what they expect from the new PM, and the unexpected quirks of the job.

We also look at plans to drop government-issued digital ID for all British adults and what he’ll do with Thames Water.

author: BBC News
description:
Andrew and Tristan Tate have been arrested in the US after British prosecutors authorised 38 new charges, taking the total number they face in the UK to 59.
 
Andrew Tate now faces 42 charges, including further counts of rape, sex trafficking and offences relating to indecent images of a child. Tristan Tate faces 17 charges, including rape and trafficking offences.
 
The brothers deny all allegations. Prosecutors have begun legal proceedings to extradite the pair, who are dual British-US citizens, to the UK.

author: BBC News
description:
The US launched another round of air strikes against Iran on Saturday night, targeting its coastal surveillance and air defence facilities, US military officials said.

It comes after two US troops were killed in a missile and drone attack in Jordan on Friday night.

The US said it targeted Iranian military sites and Revolutionary Guards forces it blames for the attack.

Iran responded with drone strikes on two US bases in Kuwait, according to state media.

The latest escalation comes after a temporary ceasefire collapsed, with both sides exchanging attacks and tensions continuing to rise across the Middle East.

description:
Computing giant Microsoft has spent 20 years pursuing an approach to quantum computing.

There is a worldwide race to develop the technology, given its potential to take on tasks currently considered too enormous for even the most powerful traditional computers.

BBC Tech Now's Adrienne Murray has rare access to Microsoft's Quantum Lab in Denmark to find out how the chips are being developed.
